title: [Core] Use numpy to speed up padded token processing (#6442)

image.wheel_note: first PyPI release after merge (2024-07-23 > 2024-07-16); picked by gen_tasks.py from PyPI upload dates.

workload.note: v0 SamplingTensors.from_lists (real classmethod) on a 256-seq penalty batch (prompts 512..1024, 128 output tokens, vocab 128256), CPU only, pinned memory off (wheel 0.5.3 torch 2.3 cu121 has no sm_120 kernels). ms per call. Author: ~50% sampler speedup at large batch on A100, no absolute numbers.

author_hardware_args.text: This small change replaces list comprehension with NumPy operations. It results in approximately a 50% speedup for the sampler when processing large batch sizes. This improvement will enhance throughput when running small models. (See bench

standalone.run_baseline: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/data/pr_6442:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=baseline vllm-task:6442 -lc 'A=/base; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 /task/bench.py'
standalone.run_pr_solution: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/data/pr_6442:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=pr_solution vllm-task:6442 -lc 'A=/gold; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 /task/bench.py'
standalone.note: The image already holds both trees (/base = baseline commit, /gold = the PR's merge commit); the one-liner swaps the chosen tree over the installed wheel exactly like run_one.sh's prelude, then runs the workload cmd from /t (the merge tree's tests/ + benchmarks/).

test_note: perf-only v0 sampler change; no test in the diff. Wheel 0.5.3 pins torch 2.3 cu121 (no sm_120 kernels): bench is CPU-only and disables pinned memory.
